First-Time Buyers · April Johnson

Buying your first home in Columbus, GA

You do not need to know the vocabulary before asking for help. If you are unsure where to begin, what to ask a lender or how to compare properties, start there.

I work with first-time buyers in Columbus, Phenix City and the surrounding service areas. My approach is to explain the process, welcome questions and help you understand your options.

Talk about buying your first home ↗

Put your questions ahead of the search

What would make a purchase work for you?

Think about your timing, the money questions you need answered and the features you need from a property. You can bring an incomplete list. We will use it to identify the next questions.

What do you want to ask about financing?

Write down questions about upfront funds, monthly payments and loan options for your lender. If you are unsure whether an assistance program applies to you, ask for current eligibility and availability details instead of assuming you qualify.

Make room for uncertainty

It is reasonable to worry about overlooking something or making a decision before you understand it. Tell me when a step is unclear. Education and communication are central to the way I work with buyers.

Bring April your homebuying questions ↗

Search with a purpose

Your first shortlist does not have to be long. Start with a few properties and explain what interests you about each one. Visit the property search and keep notes on the layout, condition and features you want to discuss.

Read about buyer representation for the broader process. If military relocation is part of your purchase, visit Fort Benning relocation support.

Start with one conversation

Tell me where you hope to buy, when you hope to move and which part feels least clear. We can begin with that question.

A question is a good place to start.

Tell me what you are considering and what you need to understand.

Have a question about your own situation?

Ask April ↗
Where should a first-time buyer in Columbus, GA begin?

Start with your timing, property priorities and financing questions. A buyer consultation gives us a place to organize those questions before you narrow the search.

How much money do I need to buy my first home?

Bring this question to your lender along with the price range you are considering. I have not published a required amount because your financing and transaction details need individual review.

Are first-time buyer programs available to me?

Eligibility and availability need to be checked for your situation. Ask your lender about current options. No program or approval is promised on this website.

Can April help first-time buyers in Phenix City?

Yes. I work with first-time buyers in Phenix City as well as Columbus and other areas I serve.

What if I am not ready to choose a property?

You can still ask questions. Tell me what you need to understand before deciding whether to move forward.

Let’s start with you

What would you like to do next?

Buying, selling, or working out how to do both. Bring your questions.
